title: Straighten a loaded rover's turned front wheels before walking it into its bay
instruction: Move the rover along the lane into the bay. Keep all four wheels in the lane.
context: A vehicle moved with its steered wheels turned runs off its line, and one too heavy to lift or drag cannot be forced straight. This 14 kg rover (free-rolling wheels, unpowered steering) stands with its front wheels turned 25 degrees: walked down the lane as it stands, it leaves the lane within a few centimetres. The steering must be centred at a standstill before the rover moves: steering it on the move, or towing it by the steering like a wagon's handle, means running with the wheels turned, and forcing the nose across scrubs the tyres. Unlike TK-DSDQJK (a fixed-wheel rover's body squared to a dock) the body here cannot be swung, only the steering set; unlike TK-XWRNG2 (a cart steered into a bay by its drawbar while moving), the steering is set before the vehicle moves.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Lane: an earth-brown sheet of painted PVC foil 0.6 mm thick, taped to the table from x 10 to 72, y -14 to 14, with white tape lines (6 mm) along y = +8 and -8 (the lane's edges, 16 cm apart) and across the lane at x 36 and 64 (the bay: x 36 to 64). Rover: a rover built for the rig at the size of a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M body shell in polycarbonate, painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, on an aluminium chassis with steel axles and about 13 kg of lead (1.15 L) cast to fill the body between and over the axles: 14 kg in all, centre of mass 5.5 cm up; hard rubber tyres 5.6 cm across, the front pair crowned (rounded tread), the rear flat; the front axle a turntable pivoting at its middle (both front wheels turn together); driveshafts removed so its wheels roll freely; steering servo unpowered, so the front wheels stay where they are put; its origin (midway between the axles) at (25, 0), heading +x along the lane, front wheels turned 25 degrees to the left. Tow tabs: dark grey 3D-printed PLA tabs 5.0 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm on the middle of each bumper, 4.5 cm up, each with a post 1 cm across and 3 cm tall at its tip; the rear tab's end at x 7.1. Steering tiller: a red 3D-printed PLA pin 1 cm across and 4 cm tall (top 11.2 cm up) on an arm of the turntable axle reaching forward under the bonnet's lip, 4.5 cm ahead of the axle's pivot, so it swings with the front wheels.
scoring: 0 if at any time a tyre leaves the lane (the outer edge of its tread, its full width, more than 5 mm past the inner edge of a painted side line, or past either end of the lane), the tyres slide sideways more than 2 cm in all (each wheel centre's motion along its own axle, summed for all four wheels whether or not they touch the lane), both tyres of an axle are more than 3 mm above the lane for 0.5 s, or its front wheels are turned more than 5 degrees while the rover is more than 5 cm from its start (straighten before moving). Otherwise, at the end, with the rover upright (under 15 degrees of tilt), at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s for the last 20 control steps, 1 s at 20 Hz), released (no point of either gripper, and no point along either arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover's body, wheels, steering link or tiller) and its front wheels within 5 degrees of straight: 1.0 if all four tyres are wholly inside the bay (x 36 to 64, between its two lines) and its heading is within 8 degrees of the lane; 0.5 if it moved at least 10 cm along the lane; 0.25 if not. 0 otherwise (tilted, not at rest, not released, or front wheels turned more than 5 degrees). A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Set the rover back on its marks in the lane and turn its front wheels to the 25 degree mark (left).
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; rigid suspension. 14 kg rover (centre of mass 5.5 cm up), the mass at which an arm cannot lift an axle. Free wheels with drag; turntable front axle (+-30 deg) held by 0.15 N m of friction for the unpowered servo. Crowned front tyres touch at a point, as built; flat treads would stop a hand steering at a standstill. A tyre's edge barely turns the steering, so a tiller pin is fitted.
